maya: Heads-up: I'm landing a tf change to move our app subnets into new /20s and introduce a NAT 'redistributor' for Cilium-managed egress. Need a quick sanity check on route table associations and PrivateLink DNS impact. Plan: update module/network/subnets.tf and module/egress/nat.tf, then terraform apply in staging. Anyone see immediate red flags? cc @liam @akash

liam: Quick Q — are we preserving the existing subnet tags (kubernetes.io/role/*)? If tags change the autoscaler or kube cloud provider might mis-detect node roles. Also, are we toggling source/dest checks on ENIs?

maya: Keeping role tags identical. Not touching S3 gateway endpoints, but adding an interface endpoint for our internal service. Concern: interface endpoints create ENIs in the subnets—will new AZ distribution reduce subnet capacity? Also need to confirm Route53 private DNS behavior. Terraform snippet I'm trying:

```resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "myservice" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = var.service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.app_subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.ep_sg.id]
  # enable_private_dns = true  # toggled off during cutover
}
```

Any quick SG suggestions?

liam: SG should allow inbound from app subnets on 443 (and 80 if needed); egress only to 443. Make sure NLB/health checks are allowed. For DNS: enabling private DNS on the endpoint creates alias records; if you already have a private zone override you can end up with conflicting records — consider applying with `enable_private_dns = false` then switch after cutover. Run `terraform plan` with the endpoint to see alias changes.

akash: One more: moving subnets may affect TGW route propagation if we rely on explicit route table IDs. Update the route_table_association resources or propagation blocks. I recommend targeting the plan to the associations first:

`terraform plan -target=module.network.aws_route_table_association.app`

then verify with `aws ec2 describe-route-tables` in staging. I can run the checks if you want.

maya: Good call. Also ran into TF state drift when subnets were replaced — ENIs attached to EKS nodes got recreated. Thinking `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on subnet resources? Concerned about Cilium egress IPs being lost since nodes get new IPs.

liam: Cilium's egress can break if node private IPs change. Safer to create new subnets and move nodegroups (rolling update) so IPs are stable per node, or use stable secondary ENIs/EIPs for NAT. Rolling node replacement is slower but less risky.

maya: Updated plan: create new subnets, update nodegroup to include new subnets, cordon/drain/rolling update nodes, verify egress IPs (Cilium) and app traffic, then decommission old subnets. For PrivateLink I'll apply with `enable_private_dns = false` until DNS is validated. I'll request infra-bot approval for staging apply.

infra-bot: Deploy check queued: PR #4523 targets module/network. CI: plan OK for staging, diff shows 3 new subnets, 2 new route_table_associations, 1 vpc_endpoint interface. Please confirm security review and maintenance window.

maya: Confirmed. Scheduling maintenance: 2026-03-22 02:00-03:00 UTC. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4523

akash: LGTM. I'll monitor TGW propagation and route tables during cutover — ping me if you see blackholed egress.

maya: Thanks everyone :rocket:
